topic: What orbital configurations justify prioritizing V-band (57-66 GHz) over optical systems for inter-satellite communication?
consensus_response: High-orbit constellations with large buffer sizes and high data rates (>10 Gbps) favor V-band (57-66 GHz) due to its higher frequency band offering better spectral efficiency and lower interference levels compared to optical links. In such cases, the V-band's wider bandwidth and higher data rate capabilities make it a more attractive option for inter-satellite communication. Additionally, V-band systems can operate with smaller buffer sizes, reducing the complexity and cost of the satellite payload.
reference_context: The reference context highlights various frequency bands and their corresponding uplink and downlink frequencies, as well as the importance of buffer size in optical links for high-orbit constellations.
